newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius rupee firms on dollar after intervention.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius rupee firms on dollar after intervention.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee firmed against both the dollar and the pound on Tuesday, reflecting the central bank's support of the local currency through market interventions, forex dealers said.
The rupee was fixed at a mean commercial rate of 20.0310 against the dollar from 20.1065 on Monday. The rupee firmed to a mean of 33.4535 against the pound from 33.5135 on Monday.
Forex dealers attributed the stronger rupee on a central bank sale of dollars below the interbank rate in a market intervention on Monday.
"The market is reflecting the supply of dollars and the central bank is having a prominent role in it. The regular interventions are supporting the rupee," one dealer said.
The central bank has been seen selling dollars in the interbank forex market at regular intervals since late October.
The view of the rupee's support by regular supply through market interventions was echoed by central bank governor Dan Maraye.
After the Monday intervention, he told Reuters the rupee's fixing against the dollar was reflecting the net trend between demand and supply on the market.
